summary: MONEYTRACE P0 login fix + WhatsApp Security Alerts feature fully verified end-to-end. Backend pytest 9/9 pass (cookie auth, /auth/me, wrong-password 401, admin /security endpoints with reviewer 403, contact CRUD with PH-mobile normalization to +63, duplicate 409, invalid phone 400, patch toggle, test send returns 'not_configured', simulate creates incident with delivery list, delete then 404, account_lockout after 5 fails + 429 on 6th + account_lockout incident recorded). Frontend Playwright: admin login redirects to /console, /console/projects loads data, nav-security visible for admin, /console/security banner 'Twilio WhatsApp is NOT configured' shown, 3 rule cards render, add-contact form works, test button shows Removed/Warning toast (not_configured), simulate-alert-button adds incident to incidents-list, delete removes contact. Reviewer login: nav-security absent, direct navigation to /console/security redirects to /console.

issues: A pill/badge showing 'REVIEWER CONSOLE' appears in the top bar even when logged in as the admin user (elijahespiritu221b@gmail.com). Sidebar and permissions are correct (Administration → Rule Configuration + Security Alerts visible, admin actions work), so this looks like a purely cosmetic mis-label of the role badge in Layout.jsx header. Should read 'ADMIN CONSOLE' for admin role.

passed: 5 wrong-password attempts for throwaway email -> 401 each, 6th -> 429 'Account temporarily locked'
POST /api/security/alerts/simulate creates incident, deliveries includes our contact
Frontend: nav-security visible only for admin; /console/security banner + 3 rule cards + add/test/simulate/delete flows work
Frontend: reviewer nav-security absent; direct /console/security redirects to /console
action_items: Cosmetic: fix role badge in the top header (Layout.jsx) to render 'ADMIN CONSOLE' for admin instead of 'REVIEWER CONSOLE'. Functionality is unaffected.
critical_code_review_comments: whatsapp_alerts.dispatch_security_alert() is invoked via asyncio.create_task inside login() but references the module-level `db`. Fine here but could double-fire if login handler is retried; consider using an event/queue if scale grows.
In-memory _ALERT_COOLDOWN and _rate_limit buckets reset on backend restart — acceptable but worth noting for multi-replica deployments (need Redis).
test_credentials: Used admin elijahespiritu221b@gmail.com and reviewer reviewer@moneytrace.gov.ph from /app/memory/test_credentials.md. Throwaway victim-test-*@x.com emails were used for the lockout test.
seed_data_creation: None. Test contacts and login_lockouts cleaned up via mongosh moneytrace_db after tests.
context_for_next_testing_agent: Backend regression file is /app/backend/tests/test_security_alerts.py (pytest, parallel-safe). It uses REACT_APP_BACKEND_URL and cleans up its own contacts. Before running, clear stale state if needed: mongosh moneytrace_db --eval 'db.login_lockouts.deleteMany({}); db.alert_contacts.deleteMany({name:/^TEST/});'. Also, do not spam login as the admin email; use random victim-test-*@x.com for lockout scenarios (per-IP throttle is 30/15min).
